institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that I considered Sciences Po one of the top places in the world to study international relations along with the fact that Paris is a city I always have wanted to try and live in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It could have been easier. Much of the important information I received from other students and friends who were in the same situation. Felt I was lucky, and would have had more trouble if I didn't know anyone.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received some emails, but not much.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It took a lot of effort, almost three months of searching.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be aware of scamming. Try to find something from someone you know who is living in the city and perhaps can pass their place onto you.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a jungle if you had not tried it before. Many of the courses were already taken by non-exchange students before the registration period. I understand that exchange students get the last pick, but it would be helpful they could plan their registration according to which courses are already full.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A short youtube introduction. But you have to know someone who tried it before.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get any of my 1st priorities, however I turned out to be very satisfied with the courses I ended up with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask someone you know who tried it before for advise.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very satisfactory. Only one course that did not really live up to my expectations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UCPH encourage more critical thinking and discussion generally. In this regard, Sciences Po is more old school with a certain distance to the professors. But it's fun to try. Additionally, mandatory physical presence is a good thing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Energy in the MENA region
Geopolitical analysis
Foundations of humanitarian action
African history since 1800
History of the global economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Energy in the MENA region: Naji was a thrill to have as a teacher, not every day you get to know a former advisor for the Qatari government. Very knowledgeable.

History of the global economy: Professor O'Rourke is one of the best lecturers I have had.

questions.answer: Books that wasn't available and that I had to buy myself.

questions.answer: Electricity and heat was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not get any sports activities even though I was ready on the minute registration started.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Run and go to London.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Took some time, but generally people are nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That all emails sent by the host institution is in French in the subjects, so it's difficult to know if it of special importance.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and general way of enjoying life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Reach out to someone who tried it before. Don't hesitate.
2. Find a good place to study, that is outside campus. A local library for example.
3. Remember to enjoy yourself and don't stress too much about exams. The level is not as high as you might think.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The general experience of living another life abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not getting any sports activities. And accidentally grabbing a homeless guy in the laundromat because I had to get my sheet that was on the floor and didn't realise he was sleeping underneath it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
